Facts, relevant for disposal of the Rule, in short, are that, the opposite party No. 1, Amir Ali and another, as plaintiffs, had filed Pre-emption Case No.67 of 2005, before the court of Senior Assistant Judge, Daudkandi, Cumilla, under the provision of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (SAT), against present opposite party No. 1, Moqbul Hossain Sarkar (the purchaser), Md Ismail (the seller) and others, seeking pre-emption in respect of 71/2 decimals of land, described in the schedule to the plaint, alleging inter-alia that, the pre-emptor-petitioners are co-sharers, by inheritance, in the suit holding and that they have right of pre-emption in the suit property lying at SA Plot No. 1396 of SA Khatian No.397 of Mouza Malihil, PS Dauddkandi District-Cumilla. It has also been stated that, the suit property belonged to SA recorded owner Foyjuddin and the seller (present opposite party No. 2) is the Nephew of the pre-emptor, who sold the suit property to the pre-emptee-opposite party No. 1, who is the petitioner before us. It has been further alleged that, the pre-emptor knowing about the said transfer filed this miscellaneous case on 11-10-2005, therefore, the pre-emptors has right of pre-emption. 

 12. I have considered the deposition of the PW 1, Md Abdul Mannan. During cross-examination he has stated that, he came to know about the transfer from Moqbul Hossain Sarkar (the pre-emptee-purchaser). He denied the suggestion that the first offer for sale was made to him or and that he had refused to purchase the suit property. The PW 2, Mojibor Rahman, in his deposition, has stated that, there is a dwelling house of Abdul Mannan and Amir Ali at the suit property. During cross-examination he has also stated that, the suit property is under their possession.
